title: Consolidated v1->v2 SDK migration guide, streaming ergonomics examples, and changelog automation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: produce a single authoritative migration guide covering v1->v2 behavioral changes across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, emphasise streaming ergonomics and retry semantics, provide end-to-end examples, and automate changelog generation for SDK releases. Deliverables: 1) migration doc that maps deprecated APIs to new equivalents + migration recipes; 2) dedicated streaming ergonomics section with canonical patterns for async iteration, backpressure, and partial results; 3) retry matrices and recommended default policies (idempotency annotations, safe retries for streams); 4) example repo snippets for each language; 5) a CI job that extracts changelog entries from PR descriptions and SDK doc comments to produce a release-note draft.
acceptance_criteria: Migration guide published in docs site under /sdk/migration with Python/TS/Go sections
At least three language-specific streaming examples (sync/async where applicable) that demonstrate resumable/partial streaming
Retry policy doc with explicit recommendations for short-lived vs long-lived requests and guidance for combining client-side and server-side retries
Automated changelog job in .github/workflows/changelog.yml that assembles CHANGELOG.md drafts from PR labels and 'changelog:' tags
Documentation reviewed and approved by Docs and SDK owners (review comments resolved)
comments: 2026-03-05 Maya Patel: Triage - initial scoping. Observed repeated support tickets where customers saw different streaming semantics between node and python clients. Proposal: canonicalize on an "iterate_responses" pattern and add helper utilities in each SDK.

2026-03-07 Luca Rossi: Engineering review - agreed on pattern but raised concern about breaking changes for current streaming API in v1. Decided to provide backwards-compatible wrappers in v2 and a clear deprecation timeline in the migration guide.
2026-03-08 Priya Shah (Docs): Draft outline uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDKs/SDK+v1+to+v2+Migration. Will convert to site markdown after reviews.

2026-03-09 Luca Rossi: Implemented initial TypeScript helper (examples/ts/stream-utils.ts). Core idea: expose both stream() returning AsyncIterable<Message> and a convenience onMessage(callback) for callback-first users. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4123

2026-03-10 Bin Wu (Go): Submitted streaming ergonomics PR that adds an iterator pattern and a 'Resume' token for long streams. Concern: serialization of resume token between heterogeneous clients. Added E2E tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/88

2026-03-11 Maya Patel: Changelog automation spike - prototype GH action extracts 'changelog: <entry>' lines from merged PR bodies and groups them by component label (python/typescript/go). Draft action at .github/workflows/changelog-draft.yml. Output written to artifacts/changelog-draft-<tag>.md

2026-03-12 Docs review: fixed language around "safe retries" vs "unsafe retries" for streaming endpoints. Added explicit note: 'do not retry mid-stream; prefer resumable streams or server-side checkpointing'. See comments on PR 4123.
2026-03-12 Luca Rossi: Next steps - finalize migration examples, wire changelog job to release pipeline, schedule a brief sync with Support on 2026-03-15 to review common customer scenarios.
notes: Migration mapping highlights: - v1 streaming callback -> v2 AsyncIterator; - 'retry' flags moved from client config to RetryPolicy object; - JSONStreamingResponse renamed to StreamResponse with unified fields: event_type, payload, resume_token

Retry recommendation summary: - short idempotent non-stream requests: exponential backoff with jitter, 3 attempts default - long-running streaming: prefer resume_token; only retry from start if idempotent and server supports stateless replay - image/large-binary transfers: use chunked upload + explicit checksums

Changelog automation: - require PRs to include a top-level line starting with 'changelog:' followed by one-line summary - GH Action groups by 'component:' label and appends to component section - maintainers must edit draft during release cut

Example Python streaming snippet (to be rendered in docs):

from redwood import SDKClient
client = SDKClient()
for chunk in client.chat.stream(model='rwd-chat-1', prompt='Tell me a story'):
    print(chunk.text)

Async variant uses 'async for' and 'client.chat.stream_async'
risk_assessment: Breaking changes risk: medium — minimized by providing wrappers and deprecation shim in v2
Operational risk: low — changelog automation reduces human error but requires maintainers to follow PR conventions
Security risk: low — no sensitive defaults changed; deprecation of old auth helpers documented separately
